The second pathway connects doxorubicin to KU-19-19, which is targeted by patupilone, also resulting in SNU1 modulation. These relationships suggest that doxorubicin exerts its effects on SNU1 through distinct molecular mechanisms, possibly involving transcriptional regulation. The integration of these pathways highlights the complexity of doxorubicin's interaction with SNU1, where different compounds act through separate but related molecular targets.
